why: ¶19 names Silas Brown as the manager of the Mapleton establishment.
¶19 says Mapleton belongs to Lord Backwater.
¶19 says the villas to the north were built by a Tavistock contractor.
¶19 mentions a few roaming gypsies inhabiting the moor.
¶19 says the northern villas were built for invalids and others seeking the Dartmoor air.
¶19 says the stable held four horses in all, so other horses besides Silver Blaze exist there.
¶19 says Tavistock lies two miles to the west.
¶19 says the Colonel's training-stable is at King's Pyland.
¶19 says the three lads who were not sitting up slept in the loft.
¶19 says Straker's villa is about two hundred yards from the stables.
¶19 names Mapleton as the larger training establishment across the moor.
¶19 describes a small cluster of villas about half a mile to the north.
Horses are central to the story so far (Silver Blaze, the four horses at King's Pyland, the Wessex Cup favourite).
¶19 says one lad sat up each night in the stable, so a lad is present.
¶19 says the other lads slept in the loft, so there are further lads beyond the one on watch.
¶19 says Straker served the Colonel five years as jockey and seven as trainer, a total of about twelve years, so service began about twelve years before.
¶19 says Straker has been trainer for seven years, so that role began about seven years before.
